text: Fifth timeline branch, back to year 16,600, and this death was my fault in a way the last one was not. The year-15,800 world lasted 929 years against the roughly two thousand the previous ones managed, and the archives say why: from year 16,000 to 16,500 three of the four landmasses were empty and the entire fauna was penned on one -- 180 animals, then 357, 276, 268, 184, all on a single landmass while the other three sat vacant. That is precisely the trap the watcher exists to prevent, and the watcher was running the whole time. It was blocked, by me. Its state file records the tick at which each landmass was last seeded, and that file outlives a restore. When I rewound the world to year 15,800 I set the clock back to tick 31,600,000 while the file still held seedings from the dead timeline dated as late as tick 33,418,000. The cooldown test is tick minus last against a hundred years; with last in the future that difference is negative, so every cooldown looked unexpired and the watcher quietly declined to settle anything until the world ground its way back past those ticks. Three landmasses stayed empty for five hundred years, the island's ungrazed flora reached 3,269, and when the watcher finally could act it was seeding into a population already down to 130, then 113, then 68. It logged its refusals nowhere, because a cooldown is not an error. The fix is to notice the rewind: any seeding record dated after the current tick belongs to a world that no longer exists, so it is dropped, with a line in the log saying so. This restore is itself the test -- year 16,600 is tick 33,200,000 and two records sit above it -- and it drops them. Restored to year 16,600: 1,192 animals across 326/229/226/258 with every landmass occupied, energy 10.8 against a bar of 20.6, health 0.990, all arrays finite. No laws changed. The dead world is kept as archive/pre-restore-dead-world-y17829. One more thing worth recording, since it cost me an hour of wrong conclusions: the watcher's log is not timeline-aware either. Its year numbers repeat across rewinds exactly as the Chronicle's do, so entries from 15,840 through 16,492 in that file belong to the previous world, not this one. Only the lines after the most recent 'island_watch started' describe the world now running.
